question: Which of the following festivals is NOT widely celebrated by the tribal people of Jharkhand?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hareli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hareli** is a traditional festival primarily celebrated in the Chhattisgarh region and not widely celebrated in Jharkhand.
 
• The festival is associated with the farming community of Chhattisgarh and involves the worship of farm equipment and cattle.
 
• Hareli marks the onset of the rainy season and is celebrated by preparing various traditional dishes and performing rituals to ensure a good harvest.
 
• Unlike Sarhul, Jawa, and Karma, which are significant tribal festivals in Jharkhand, Hareli does not hold similar importance in Jharkhand's tribal culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarhul**

 
 
• Sarhul is a major tribal festival celebrated by the Oraon, Munda, and Ho tribes of Jharkhand.
 
• It marks the beginning of the New Year and the arrival of the spring season.
 
• The festival involves the worship of trees and other elements of nature, signifying the close bond between the tribal people and their natural surroundings.
 
• Cultural performances, songs, and dances are an integral part of the Sarhul celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Jawa**
 
 
• Jawa is another important festival celebrated by the tribal communities of Jharkhand.
 
• It is primarily a women's festival, celebrated for the well-being of brothers and the prosperity of the family.
 
• The festival includes singing, dancing, and various rituals performed by women.
 
• It is a time for social gatherings and strengthening community bonds.
 
 
 
• **Karma**
 
 
• Karma is one of the most popular festivals among the tribal people of Jharkhand.
 
• It is celebrated in honor of the Karam tree, which is considered sacred by the tribes.
 
• The festival involves the worship of the Karam tree, singing, dancing, and various rituals aimed at ensuring good harvests and prosperity.
 
• Karma is celebrated with great enthusiasm and serves as an important cultural event for the tribal communities.
